configuration: The upstream example program examples/geometry-models.cpp, on the ur5 description it already names, vendored with the pinned source at code/pinocchio/models/example-robot-data/robots/ur_description/. It parses the description into a Model and into two GeometryModels, one holding the collision shapes and one the visual shapes, runs the forward kinematics at a configuration and places every geometry object of both models in the world. The configuration is read from ic/<ic>/operands.json; upstream draws it from randomConfiguration, which takes the unseeded std::rand stream inside the module a solver would port. Graded: the placement of every joint and of every collision and visual geometry object, at full binary64 precision rather than the two decimal places the example prints.
observable: the joint placements and the collision and visual geometry placements the example prints
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the configuration is an initial condition in ic/ rather than a random draw, and that main() is wrapped as a test case so that the leaf's one adapter shape applies
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero number of ic/nominal/operands.json; the zeros are left as they are, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is not a perturbation of a length, an angle or a quaternion coordinate. Perturbing every nonzero component rather than one component per quantity is deliberate: on an earlier Pinocchio leaf, moving a single entry of a rotation rounded away in an output built from all nine and left dozens of observables with a spread of exactly zero, while moving all of them is still a two-ulp calibration. Here that is the six joint angles of the arm, which are the example's only input. All 6 numbers of ic/nominal/operands.json move; none of them is zero. The worst measured spread over all 264 graded values is 1.3878e-15 absolute. 3 of the 22 observables show a spread of exactly zero: collision_oMg_base_link_0, joint_placement_universe, visual_oMg_base_link_0. They are structurally constant rather than insensitive, and the warrant says why; their bound rests on that physical argument rather than on a measured sensitivity.
altbuild: none: the same source built at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off reproduces the -O2 -DNDEBUG result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. The graded quantities are rigid transform compositions and geometric distances between fixed shapes; Eigen fixes the evaluation order of the expressions, the loops are scalar, and coal's shape queries are closed form or an exhaustive minimum over a fixed set of features, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate. The alternative build was nevertheless run for every check of this leaf rather than assumed, because on an earlier Pinocchio leaf it was what exposed a graded buffer that was reading uninitialised memory.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned library, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead.

warrant: The graded quantities are the placement of every joint of the kinematic tree and of every collision and visual geometry object, in metres and in the model's Cartesian axes, named after the joint or the geometry object, both of which the description fixes. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 1.00e+00, it admits about 1.01e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this program can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a geometry object placed from the wrong joint, a visual model given the collision model's placements, or a transform composed in the wrong order moves entries by order one, fifteen decades above the bound. Three graded records do not move under the variant and are structurally constant rather than insensitive: the universe joint's placement is the identity by definition, and the base link's collision and visual objects are rigidly attached to it at the identity in a fixed-base model, so no configuration can move them. They are kept because they are rows of the table the example prints, and a port that moved them would be wrong; their bound rests on that argument rather than on a measured sensitivity, and the curator should read it as such. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these compositions differs by about a few units in the last place of the largest intermediate, some 1e-15 in these units, six decades inside the bound, and because the alternative build measured exactly zero. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst graded value by 1.3878e-15, using 1.381e-06 of the bound, that is 724,176 times of headroom across all 264 graded values; and every graded value scaled by 0.1 per cent, a fault far smaller than any this test can express, is rejected at 990,099 times the bound. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
